gloss: entry into port; arriving at a port

definitions.gloss: entry into port; arriving at a port
definitions.explanation: The act of a ship entering and arriving at a harbor or port. Used in maritime, logistics, and travel contexts.

examples.japanese: {大型|おおがた}{船|せん}が{入港|にゅうこう}した。
examples.english: A large ship entered the port.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}の{影響|えいきょう}で{入港|にゅうこう}が{遅|おく}れている。
examples.english: Port entry has been delayed due to the typhoon.

examples.japanese: クルーズ{船|せん}が{横浜港|よこはまこう}に{入港|にゅうこう}し、{多|おお}くの{観光客|かんこうきゃく}が{下船|げせん}した。
examples.english: A cruise ship entered the port of Yokohama, and many tourists disembarked.

notes:
USAGE: {入港|にゅうこう} is used as a noun or with する. It applies to all types of vessels — cargo ships, cruise ships, military ships, and fishing boats.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- AがBに{入港|にゅうこう}する (A enters port B)
- Aへの{入港|にゅうこう} (entry into port A)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {入港|にゅうこう}{許可|きょか} (port entry permit)
- {入港|にゅうこう}{手続|てつづ}き (port entry procedures)
- {入港|にゅうこう}{予定|よてい} (scheduled port arrival)

The antonym is {出港|しゅっこう} (departure from port). Together, {入港|にゅうこう} and {出港|しゅっこう} describe the arrival and departure of vessels.
